title: Two Sum II
kidExplanation: A sorted row of coins. Two fingers — one at each end — hunt for a pair that hits the target sum.
plainProblem: Two Sum II: A sorted row of coins. Worked example — input: numbers = [2,7,11,15], target = 9; expected output: [1,2]. Why: 1-indexed. Interview pattern to name out loud: Two pointers from both ends (or slow/fast).

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Two Sum II”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input numbers = [2,7,11,15], target = 9 should still produce [1,2].

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: O(n).

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: The input array 'numbers' is already sorted in non-decreasing order. To find the two numbers that add up to the target, we can use a two-pointer approach. We initialize two pointers, one at the beginning of the array (left) and the other at the end of the array (right). We then check the sum of the elements at these two pointers. If the sum is equal to the target, we have found the pair. If the sum is less than the target, it means we need to increase the sum, so we move the left pointer one step to the right. If the sum is greater than the target, it means we need to decrease the sum, so we move the right pointer one step to the left. We continue this process until we find the pair or the two pointers meet or cross each other.
